verses.pali: Majjhima Nikāya 152
verses.english: Middle Discourses 152

verses.pali: Indriyabhāvanāsutta
verses.english: The Development of the Faculties

verses.pali: Evaṁ me sutaṁ—
verses.english: So I have heard.

verses.pali: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā gajaṅgalāyaṁ viharati suveḷuvane.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kajaṅgalā in a bamboo grove.

verses.pali: Atha kho uttaro māṇavo pārāsiviyantevāsī yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodi.
verses.english: Then the student Uttara, a pupil of the brahmin Pārāsariya, approached the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him.

verses.pali: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho uttaraṁ māṇavaṁ pārāsiviyantevāsiṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
verses.english: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him,

verses.pali: “deseti, uttara, pārāsiviyo brāhmaṇo sāvakānaṁ indriyabhāvanan”ti?
verses.english: “Uttara, does Pārāsariya teach his disciples the development of the faculties?”

verses.pali: “Deseti, bho gotama, pārāsiviyo brāhmaṇo sāvakānaṁ indriyabhāvanan”ti.
verses.english: “He does, worthy Gotama.”

verses.pali: “Yathā kathaṁ pana, uttara, deseti pārāsiviyo brāhmaṇo sāvakānaṁ indriyabhāvanan”ti?
verses.english: “But how does he teach it?”

verses.pali: “Idha, bho gotama, cakkhunā rūpaṁ na passati, sotena saddaṁ na suṇāti—
verses.english: “Worthy Gotama, it’s when the eye sees no sight and the ear hears no sound.

verses.pali: evaṁ kho, bho gotama, deseti pārāsiviyo brāhmaṇo sāvakānaṁ indriyabhāvanan”ti.
verses.english: That’s how Pārāsariya teaches his disciples the development of the faculties.”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ sante kho, uttara, andho bhāvitindriyo bhavissati, badhiro bhāvitindriyo bhavissati;
verses.english: “In that case, Uttara, a blind person and a deaf person will have developed faculties

verses.pali: yathā pārāsiviyassa brāhmaṇassa vacanaṁ.
verses.english: according to what Pārāsariya says.

verses.pali: Andho hi, uttara, cakkhunā rūpaṁ na passati, badhiro sotena saddaṁ na suṇātī”ti.
verses.english: For a blind person sees no sight with the eye and a deaf person hears no sound with the ear.”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, uttaro māṇavo pārāsiviyantevāsī tuṇhībhūto maṅkubhūto pattakkhandho adhomukho pajjhāyanto appaṭibhāno nisīdi.
verses.english: When he said this, Uttara sat silent, dismayed, shoulders drooping, downcast, depressed, with nothing to say.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā uttaraṁ māṇavaṁ pārāsiviyantevāsiṁ tuṇhībhūtaṁ maṅkubhūtaṁ pattakkhandhaṁ adhomukhaṁ pajjhāyantaṁ appaṭibhānaṁ viditvā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ āmantesi:
verses.english: Knowing this, the Buddha addressed Venerable Ānanda,

verses.pali: “aññathā kho, ānanda, deseti pārāsiviyo brāhmaṇo sāvakānaṁ indriyabhāvanaṁ, aññathā ca panānanda, ariyassa vinaye anuttarā indriyabhāvanā hotī”ti.
verses.english: “Ānanda, the development of the faculties taught by Pārāsariya is quite different from the supreme development of the faculties in the training of the Noble One.”

verses.pali: “Etassa, bhagavā, kālo; etassa, sugata, kālo
verses.english: “Now is the time, Blessed One! Now is the time, Holy One.

verses.pali: yaṁ bhagavā ariyassa vinaye anuttaraṁ indriyabhāvanaṁ deseyya. Bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī”ti.
verses.english: Let the Buddha teach the supreme development of the faculties in the training of the Noble One. The mendicants will listen and remember it.”

verses.pali: “Tenahānanda, suṇāhi, sādhukaṁ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti.
verses.english: “Well then, Ānanda, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato paccassosi.
verses.english: “Yes, sir,” Ānanda replied.

verses.pali: Bhagavā etadavoca:
verses.english: The Buddha said this:

verses.pali: “Kathañcānanda, ariyassa vinaye anuttarā indriyabhāvanā hoti?
verses.english: “And how, Ānanda, is there the supreme development of the faculties in the training of the Noble One?

verses.pali: Idhānanda, bhikkhuno cakkhunā rūpaṁ disvā uppajjati manāpaṁ, uppajjati amanāpaṁ, uppajjati manāpāmanāpaṁ.
verses.english: When a mendicant sees a sight with their eyes, in them arises what is agreeable, what is disagreeable, and what is both agreeable and disagreeable.

verses.pali: So evaṁ pajānāti:
verses.english: They understand:

verses.pali: ‘uppannaṁ kho me idaṁ manāpaṁ, uppannaṁ amanāpaṁ, uppannaṁ manāpāmanāpaṁ.
verses.english: ‘What is agreeable, what is disagreeable, and what is both agreeable and disagreeable have arisen in me.

verses.pali: Tañca kho saṅkhataṁ oḷārikaṁ paṭiccasamuppannaṁ.
verses.english: That’s conditioned, crude, and dependently originated.

verses.pali: Etaṁ santaṁ etaṁ paṇītaṁ yadidaṁ—
verses.english: But this is peaceful and sublime, namely

verses.pali: upekkhā’ti.
verses.english: equanimity.’

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ uppannaṁ manāpaṁ uppannaṁ amanāpaṁ uppannaṁ manāpāmanāpaṁ nirujjhati;
verses.english: Then the agreeable, the disagreeable, and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose in them cease,

verses.pali: upekkhā saṇṭhāti.
verses.english: and equanimity becomes stabilized.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, ānanda, cakkhumā puriso ummīletvā vā nimīleyya, nimīletvā vā ummīleyya;
verses.english: It’s like how a person with clear eyes might open their eyes then shut them; or might shut their eyes then open them.

verses.pali: evameva kho, ānanda, yassa kassaci evaṁsīghaṁ evaṁtuvaṭaṁ evaṁappakasirena uppannaṁ manāpaṁ uppannaṁ amanāpaṁ uppannaṁ manāpāmanāpaṁ nirujjhati, upekkhā saṇṭhāti—
verses.english: Such is the speed, the swiftness, the ease with which anything agreeable, disagreeable, and both agreeable and disagreeable that arose in them cease, and equanimity becomes stabilized.

verses.pali: ayaṁ vuccatānanda, ariyassa vinaye anuttarā indriyabhāvanā cakkhuviññeyyesu rūpesu.
verses.english: In the training of the Noble One this is called the supreme development of the faculties regarding sights known by the eye.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, ānanda, bhikkhuno sotena saddaṁ sutvā uppajjati manāpaṁ, uppajjati amanāpaṁ, uppajjati manāpāmanāpaṁ.
verses.english: Furthermore, when a mendicant hears a sound with their ears, the agreeable, the disagreeable, and the both agreeable and disagreeable arise in them.

verses.pali: So evaṁ pajānāti:
verses.english: They understand:

verses.pali: ‘uppannaṁ kho me idaṁ manāpaṁ, uppannaṁ amanāpaṁ, uppannaṁ manāpāmanāpaṁ.
verses.english: ‘What is agreeable, what is disagreeable, and what is both agreeable and disagreeable have arisen in me.

verses.pali: Tañca kho saṅkhataṁ oḷārikaṁ paṭiccasamuppannaṁ.
verses.english: That’s conditioned, crude, and dependently originated.

verses.pali: Etaṁ santaṁ etaṁ paṇītaṁ yadidaṁ—
verses.english: But this is peaceful and sublime, namely

verses.pali: upekkhā’ti.
verses.english: equanimity.’

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ uppannaṁ manāpaṁ uppannaṁ amanāpaṁ uppannaṁ manāpāmanāpaṁ nirujjhati;
verses.english: Then the agreeable, the disagreeable, and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose in them cease,

verses.pali: upekkhā saṇṭhāti.
verses.english: and equanimity becomes stabilized.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, ānanda, balavā puriso appakasireneva accharaṁ pahareyya;
verses.english: It’s like how a strong person can effortlessly snap their fingers.

verses.pali: evameva kho, ānanda, yassa kassaci evaṁsīghaṁ evaṁtuvaṭaṁ evaṁappakasirena uppannaṁ manāpaṁ uppannaṁ amanāpaṁ uppannaṁ manāpāmanāpaṁ nirujjhati, upekkhā saṇṭhāti—
verses.english: Such is the speed, the swiftness, the ease with which anything agreeable, disagreeable, and both agreeable and disagreeable that arose in them cease, and equanimity becomes stabilized.

verses.pali: ayaṁ vuccatānanda, ariyassa vinaye anuttarā indriyabhāvanā sotaviññeyyesu saddesu.
verses.english: In the training of the Noble One this is called the supreme development of the faculties regarding sounds known by the ear.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, ānanda, bhikkhuno ghānena gandhaṁ ghāyitvā uppajjati manāpaṁ, uppajjati amanāpaṁ, uppajjati manāpāmanāpaṁ.
verses.english: Furthermore, when a mendicant smells an odor with their nose, the agreeable, the disagreeable, and the both agreeable and disagreeable arise in them.

verses.pali: So evaṁ pajānāti:
verses.english: They understand:

verses.pali: ‘uppannaṁ kho me idaṁ manāpaṁ, uppannaṁ amanāpaṁ, uppannaṁ manāpāmanāpaṁ.
verses.english: ‘What is agreeable, what is disagreeable, and what is both agreeable and disagreeable have arisen in me.

verses.pali: Tañca kho saṅkhataṁ oḷārikaṁ paṭiccasamuppannaṁ.
verses.english: That’s conditioned, crude, and dependently originated.

verses.pali: Etaṁ santaṁ etaṁ paṇītaṁ yadidaṁ—
verses.english: But this is peaceful and sublime, namely

verses.pali: upekkhā’ti.
verses.english: equanimity.’

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ uppannaṁ manāpaṁ uppannaṁ amanāpaṁ uppannaṁ manāpāmanāpaṁ nirujjhati;
verses.english: Then the agreeable, the disagreeable, and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose in them cease,

verses.pali: upekkhā saṇṭhāti.
verses.english: and equanimity becomes stabilized.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, ānanda, īsakampoṇe padumapalāse udakaphusitāni pavattanti, na saṇṭhanti;
verses.english: It’s like how a drop of water would roll off a gently sloping lotus leaf, and would not stay there.

verses.pali: evameva kho, ānanda, yassa kassaci evaṁsīghaṁ evaṁtuvaṭaṁ evaṁappakasirena uppannaṁ manāpaṁ uppannaṁ amanāpaṁ uppannaṁ manāpāmanāpaṁ nirujjhati, upekkhā saṇṭhāti—
verses.english: Such is the speed, the swiftness, the ease with which anything agreeable, disagreeable, and both agreeable and disagreeable that arose in them cease, and equanimity becomes stabilized.

verses.pali: ayaṁ vuccatānanda, ariyassa vinaye anuttarā indriyabhāvanā ghānaviññeyyesu gandhesu.
verses.english: In the training of the Noble One this is called the supreme development of the faculties regarding smells known by the nose.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, ānanda, bhikkhuno jivhāya rasaṁ sāyitvā uppajjati manāpaṁ, uppajjati amanāpaṁ, uppajjati manāpāmanāpaṁ.
verses.english: Furthermore, when a mendicant tastes a flavor with their tongue, the agreeable, the disagreeable, and the both agreeable and disagreeable arise in them.

verses.english: They understand:

verses.pali: ‘uppannaṁ kho me idaṁ manāpaṁ, uppannaṁ amanāpaṁ, uppannaṁ manāpāmanāpaṁ.
verses.english: ‘What is agreeable, what is disagreeable, and what is both agreeable and disagreeable have arisen in me.

verses.english: That’s conditioned, crude, and dependently originated.

verses.pali: Etaṁ santaṁ etaṁ paṇītaṁ yadidaṁ—
verses.english: But this is peaceful and sublime, namely

verses.pali: upekkhā’ti.
verses.english: equanimity.’

verses.english: Then the agreeable, the disagreeable, and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose in them cease,

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, ānanda, balavā puriso jivhagge kheḷapiṇḍaṁ saṁyūhitvā appakasirena vameyya;
verses.english: It’s like how a strong person who’s formed a glob of spit on the tip of their tongue could easily spit it out.

verses.pali: evameva kho, ānanda, yassa kassaci evaṁsīghaṁ evaṁtuvaṭaṁ evaṁappakasirena uppannaṁ manāpaṁ uppannaṁ amanāpaṁ uppannaṁ manāpāmanāpaṁ nirujjhati, upekkhā saṇṭhāti—
verses.english: Such is the speed, the swiftness, the ease with which anything agreeable, disagreeable, and both agreeable and disagreeable that arose in them cease, and equanimity becomes stabilized.

verses.pali: ayaṁ vuccatānanda, ariyassa vinaye anuttarā indriyabhāvanā jivhāviññeyyesu rasesu.
verses.english: In the training of the Noble One this is called the supreme development of the faculties regarding tastes known by the tongue.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, ānanda, bhikkhuno kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṁ phusitvā uppajjati manāpaṁ, uppajjati amanāpaṁ, uppajjati manāpāmanāpaṁ.
verses.english: Furthermore, when a mendicant feels a touch with their body, the agreeable, the disagreeable, and the both agreeable and disagreeable arise in them.

verses.pali: So evaṁ pajānāti:
verses.english: They understand:

verses.pali: ‘uppannaṁ kho me idaṁ manāpaṁ, uppannaṁ amanāpaṁ, uppannaṁ manāpāmanāpaṁ.
verses.english: ‘What is agreeable, what is disagreeable, and what is both agreeable and disagreeable have arisen in me.

verses.english: That’s conditioned, crude, and dependently originated.

verses.english: But this is peaceful and sublime, namely

verses.pali: upekkhā’ti.
verses.english: equanimity.’

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ uppannaṁ manāpaṁ uppannaṁ amanāpaṁ uppannaṁ manāpāmanāpaṁ nirujjhati;
verses.english: Then the agreeable, the disagreeable, and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose in them cease,

verses.english: and equanimity becomes stabilized.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, ānanda, balavā puriso samiñjitaṁ vā bāhaṁ pasāreyya, pasāritaṁ vā bāhaṁ samiñjeyya;
verses.english: It’s like how a strong person can extend or contract their arm.

verses.pali: evameva kho, ānanda, yassa kassaci evaṁsīghaṁ evaṁtuvaṭaṁ evaṁappakasirena uppannaṁ manāpaṁ uppannaṁ amanāpaṁ uppannaṁ manāpāmanāpaṁ nirujjhati, upekkhā saṇṭhāti—

verses.pali: ayaṁ vuccatānanda, ariyassa vinaye anuttarā indriyabhāvanā kāyaviññeyyesu phoṭṭhabbesu.
verses.english: In the training of the Noble One this is called the supreme development of the faculties regarding touches known by the body.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, ānanda, bhikkhuno manasā dhammaṁ viññāya uppajjati manāpaṁ, uppajjati amanāpaṁ, uppajjati manāpāmanāpaṁ.
verses.english: Furthermore, when a mendicant knows a thought with their mind, the agreeable, the disagreeable, and the both agreeable and disagreeable arise in them.

verses.pali: So evaṁ pajānāti:
verses.english: They understand:

verses.pali: ‘uppannaṁ kho me idaṁ manāpaṁ, uppannaṁ amanāpaṁ, uppannaṁ manāpāmanāpaṁ.
verses.english: ‘What is agreeable, what is disagreeable, and what is both agreeable and disagreeable have arisen in me.

verses.pali: Tañca kho saṅkhataṁ oḷārikaṁ paṭiccasamuppannaṁ.
verses.english: That’s conditioned, crude, and dependently originated.

verses.pali: Etaṁ santaṁ etaṁ paṇītaṁ yadidaṁ—
verses.english: But this is peaceful and sublime, namely

verses.pali: upekkhā’ti.
verses.english: equanimity.’

verses.english: Then the agreeable, the disagreeable, and the both agreeable and disagreeable that arose in them cease,

verses.english: It’s like how a strong person could let two or three drops of water fall onto an iron cauldron that had been heated all day.

verses.pali: Dandho, ānanda, udakaphusitānaṁ nipāto, atha kho naṁ khippameva parikkhayaṁ pariyādānaṁ gaccheyya;
verses.english: The drops would be slow to fall, but they’d quickly dry up and evaporate.

verses.pali: evameva kho, ānanda, yassa kassaci evaṁsīghaṁ evaṁtuvaṭaṁ evaṁappakasirena uppannaṁ manāpaṁ uppannaṁ amanāpaṁ uppannaṁ manāpāmanāpaṁ nirujjhati, upekkhā saṇṭhāti—

verses.english: In the training of the Noble One this is called the supreme development of the faculties regarding ideas known by the mind.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, ānanda, ariyassa vinaye anuttarā indriyabhāvanā hoti.
verses.english: That’s how there is the supreme development of the faculties in the training of the Noble One.

verses.english: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive,’ that’s what they do.

verses.english: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive and the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do.

verses.pali: Sace ākaṅkhati: ‘appaṭikūle ca paṭikūle ca paṭikūlasaññī vihareyyan’ti, paṭikūlasaññī tattha viharati.
verses.english: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive and the repulsive,’ that’s what they do.

verses.english: If they wish: ‘May I meditate staying equanimous, mindful and aware, shunning both the repulsive and the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do.

verses.pali: kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṁ phusitvā …
verses.english: When they feel a touch with their body …

verses.pali: manasā dhammaṁ viññāya uppajjati manāpaṁ, uppajjati amanāpaṁ, uppajjati manāpāmanāpaṁ.
verses.english: When they know a thought with their mind, the agreeable, the disagreeable, and the both agreeable and disagreeable arise in them.

verses.pali: So sace ākaṅkhati: ‘paṭikūle appaṭikūlasaññī vihareyyan’ti, appaṭikūlasaññī tattha viharati.
verses.english: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive,’ that’s what they do.

verses.pali: Sace ākaṅkhati: ‘appaṭikūle paṭikūlasaññī vihareyyan’ti, paṭikūlasaññī tattha viharati.
verses.english: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do.

verses.pali: Sace ākaṅkhati: ‘paṭikūle ca appaṭikūle ca appaṭikūlasaññī vihareyyan’ti, appaṭikūlasaññī tattha viharati.
verses.english: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the unrepulsive in the repulsive and the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do.

verses.pali: Sace ākaṅkhati: ‘appaṭikūle ca paṭikūle ca paṭikūlasaññī vihareyyan’ti, paṭikūlasaññī tattha viharati.
verses.english: If they wish: ‘May I meditate perceiving the repulsive in the unrepulsive and the repulsive,’ that’s what they do.

verses.pali: Sace ākaṅkhati: ‘paṭikūlañca appaṭikūlañca tadubhayampi abhinivajjetvā upekkhako vihareyyaṁ sato sampajāno’ti, upekkhako tattha viharati sato sampajāno.
verses.english: If they wish: ‘May I meditate staying equanimous, mindful and aware, shunning both the repulsive and the unrepulsive,’ that’s what they do.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, ānanda, ariyo hoti bhāvitindriyo.
verses.english: That’s how they are a noble one with developed faculties.

verses.pali: Iti kho, ānanda, desitā mayā ariyassa vinaye anuttarā indriyabhāvanā, desito sekho pāṭipado, desito ariyo bhāvitindriyo.
verses.english: So, Ānanda, I have taught the supreme development of the faculties in the training of the Noble One, I have taught the practicing trainee, and I have taught the noble one with developed faculties.

verses.pali: Yaṁ kho, ānanda, satthārā karaṇīyaṁ sāvakānaṁ hitesinā anukampakena anukampaṁ upādāya, kataṁ vo taṁ mayā.
verses.english: Out of sympathy, I’ve done what a teacher should do who wants what’s best for their disciples.

verses.pali: Etāni, ānanda, rukkhamūlāni, etāni suññāgārāni, jhāyathānanda, mā pamādattha, mā pacchā vippaṭisārino ahuvattha. Ayaṁ vo amhākaṁ anusāsanī”ti.
verses.english: Here are these roots of trees, and here are these empty huts. Practice absorption, Ānanda! Don’t be negligent! Don’t regret it later! This is my instruction to you.”

verses.pali: Idamavoca bhagavā.
verses.english: That is what the Buddha said.

verses.pali: Attamano āyasmā ānando bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinandīti.
verses.english: Satisfied, Venerable Ānanda approved what the Buddha said.

verses.pali: Indriyabhāvanāsuttaṁ niṭṭhitaṁ dasamaṁ.
Saḷāyatanavaggo niṭṭhito pañcamo.
Tassuddānaṁ
Anāthapiṇḍiko channo,
puṇṇo nandakarāhulā;
Chachakkaṁ saḷāyatanikaṁ,
nagaravindeyyasuddhikā;
Indriyabhāvanā cāpi,
vaggo ovādapañcamoti.
Idaṁ vaggānamuddānaṁ
Devadahonupado ca,
Suññato ca vibhaṅgako;
Saḷāyatanoti vaggā,
Uparipaṇṇāsake ṭhitāti.
Uparipaṇṇāsakaṁ samattaṁ.
Tīhi paṇṇāsakehi paṭimaṇḍito sakalo
majjhimanikāyo samatto.
verses.english: The Middle Discourses are completed.
